messages:
maya: heads-up — ran into a nasty double-side-effect when streaming generation and the connection got a 502 during chunking. saving here in case it helps anyone debugging.
kevin: ugh. got a repro? streaming + resume logic is pretty new in py-sdk, right? :eyes: 
maya: quick sketch: async stream yields a few chunks, server 502 mid-stream, client retries the request without idempotency token because it thought stream wasn't accepted. server replays from start -> duplicate side-effect.
kevin: oh — so the server treats the resumed request as a fresh generate. do we have a streaming resume token today?
maya: no, current api only has idempotency_key on create endpoints. streaming path was assumed non-mutating but many customers do side-effecting ops in on_chunk.
taylor: can you paste minimal repro?
maya: sure:
```python
# minimal async repro (simplified)
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key="X")
async def run():
    async with client.stream_generate(prompt="do side effect") as s:
        async for chunk in s:
            process(chunk)  # user-defined side effect
```
If connection drops after first two chunks and client retries the whole stream, process() runs again.
raj: interesting edgecase. so client retry/backoff sees transport error and retries. The problem is the server doesn't have resume semantics + user callback runs on each chunk.
kevin: two ideas: 1) introduce a streamed-idempotency header that persists across stream retries so server can dedupe. 2) make the client surface a `stream_attempt` flag to callback so SDK consumers can guard.
maya: I prototyped option 2 in my head — callback signature: `on_chunk(chunk, attempt=0)` and `attempt>0` should be treated as a replay. But that breaks typing and will be a backwards-incompatible change for the callback protocol.
olivia: another approach — SDK could buffer a small prefix of chunks and only call user callbacks once a safe threshold is reached (e.g., after first successful full-frame). But that increases latency.
kevin: both tradeoffs. buffering shifts latency; attempt flag changes typing/contract. Could we add an opt-in `replay_protection` config in client? default off, opt-in for users who need dedupe?
raj: we should also consider server-side: accept `X-Stream-Id` and return `X-Resume-Offset` so retries can resume where left off. That requires server changes but is cleaner semantics.
maya: agreed. for short-term patch, I'm thinking to: a) add `on_chunk_attempt` param (opt-in) that forwards attempt count but doesn't change existing `on_chunk` signature. b) emit telemetry metric `stream.replay.detected` when client retries after partial receipt.
taylor: that keeps backwards compat. For typing, add an overload:
```py
# existing
def on_chunk(chunk: str) -> None: ...
# opt-in
def on_chunk_attempt(chunk: str, attempt: int) -> None: ...
```
kevin: how will users opt in? constructor flag `replay_protection='callback_attempts' | 'buffer' | None`?
maya: yeah something like `AsyncClient(..., stream_replay_policy='attempt_flag')` with doc examples.
olivia: any perf benchmarks? buffering could increase p95 by 20-40ms depending on chunk size. Need numbers.
raj: also add strong test covering flaky transport: simulate server returning 502 after N chunks and assert callback invoked only once when policy=buffer, and invoked with attempt>0 when policy=attempt_flag.
maya: I'll open a sketch PR with tests + docs. tagging kevin for SDK review and raj for server API proposal.
kevin: ack. FYI deploy-bot rolled out py-sdk v0.9.7 yesterday — that build doesn't have replay_protection. we'll aim for v0.9.8 with opt-in.
deploy-bot: release note: py-sdk v0.9.7 deployed to pypi at 2024-11-02T12:30:00Z.
maya: quick note: telemetry will help us see how common this is in prod. I'm going to add a lightweight metric before changing API surface.
taylor: assign owner?
maya: I'll own the client patch. kevin will review. raj will draft server resume header proposal. olivia can run perf bench.
kevin: sounds good. thanks for reporting and writing repro. :thumbsup:
maya: np — leaving the repro snippet and test plan in the GH issue I'm about to open. I'll post link here when created.
kevin: ping us once PR is up.
maya: GH: opened redwood/redwood-py#1423 with draft tests and docs. link: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-py/pull/1423 :rocket:
